A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same LIT-LVM research. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and support reliable matching despite pagination and organizational changes.

before.justification: v1 reports original simulation experiments, evaluations on 12 regression and 10 classification datasets, and kidney-transplant survival and HLA compatibility analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains these original results and adds hierarchical-lasso comparisons, optimization convergence plots, and an additional regularization sensitivity experiment.

M1.justification: The low-rank and latent-distance models, regularized objective, Adam/proximal optimization, and targeted-interaction masking remain unchanged. Specifying the large penalty used to approximate sparse FMs clarifies an existing comparator implementation rather than changing LIT-LVM.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same synthetic scenarios, 12 OpenML regression datasets, 10 classification datasets, and transplant application. Jasmine's newly added dataset-description row documents coverage already demonstrated in v1 Table 2. The new appendix analyses reuse existing datasets.

E2.justification: Tables 1–2 add hierarchical lasso with weak heredity across the OpenML regression and classification evaluations, substantially extending comparison to another structured-regularization family. Renaming FM to Sparse FM clarifies the existing comparator; simulation and transplant comparator membership remains unchanged.

E3.justification: The new hierarchical-lasso evaluation specifies a regularization grid, an L2 penalty of 10^-8 times lambda, and exclusion of self-interactions. Appendix C.3 adds a clean2 sweep from lambda_l = 10^5 through 10^8. Existing splits, metrics, and LIT-LVM/FM dimension settings are retained.

E4.justification: New Appendix C.2 examines training and validation loss convergence on nine classification datasets. Appendix C.3 tests whether prediction accuracy stabilizes at the large penalties used for the FM approximation. Existing dimension, noise, sparsity, regularization, and HLA analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions retain mean and standard-error reporting over five OpenML splits and ten transplant splits, together with one-standard-error simulation bars. The new comparator follows the existing reporting convention. No new seed information, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, or statistical tests are specified.

E6.justification: Tables 1–2 add hierarchical-lasso results throughout the benchmark suite; for example, clean2 AUC is 0.978 ± 0.001 against the retained LIT-LVM value of 0.985 ± 0.001. Figures 15–16 add convergence and large-penalty stability findings. Existing performance values are retained apart from rounding; corrections include Boston's reported p²/n and the RSF IBS stated in prose.

T1.justification: Section 2.2.1 newly formalizes strong heredity: a nonzero interaction coefficient requires both corresponding main-effect coefficients to be nonzero. Weak heredity is also specified for the added comparator. LIT-LVM's equations and Appendix A complexity derivations remain unchanged, with no new theorem or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract extends the predictive-superiority claim to hierarchical lasso. The introduction explicitly distinguishes LIT-LVM from heredity assumptions and sharpens its positioning among regularized and factorized predictors. The central contribution and claimed benefits of prediction and interpretable latent representations remain intact.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations of hierarchical-lasso behavior, explains the distance term's relationship to coefficient signs, and explicitly limits scalability to thousands of features. It interprets the new diagnostics as supporting optimization and FM approximation. The transplant discussion changes from matching to outperforming RSF despite unchanged Table 3 values.

D1.justification: v2 newly specifies lambda_l = 100,000 for the existing sparse-FM approximation, documents the hierNet R implementation and tuning choices, and supplies jasmine's sample count, feature count, and dataset ID. Existing tuning details move to Appendix C.1.2; the code-access information is substantively unchanged.

R1.justification: The research positioning substantially expands to distinguish LIT-LVM from heredity-based interaction selection, including Bien, Zhao, Yuan, Choi, and Radchenko and James. Further additions discuss FaStR, additive higher-order FMs, signed latent-distance models, and ultrahigh-dimensional interaction estimation. These are substantive additions beyond bibliographic cleanup.

P1.justification: The overall narrative and main section structure remain recognizable. Targeted revisions expand the introduction and related work, enumerate the comparison methods, clarify Sparse FM terminology, relocate hyperparameter details, and insert two appendix subsections. Most existing methodological and experimental prose is retained.

P2.justification: v2 adds Figures 15–16 and hierarchical-lasso columns in Tables 1–2, moves p²/n columns to Tables 4–5, and completes the jasmine description row. Existing graphics are retained with resizing, relocation, or renumbering. Table 1 adopts two-decimal formatting, rounding several nonzero standard errors to 0.00.

improvement.justification: The hierarchical-lasso comparisons fill a relevant comparator gap, while Appendices C.2–C.3 add useful optimization and approximation checks. Clearer implementation details, dataset documentation, and scalability limits improve assessability. These gains are incremental: the clean2 AUC plateau provides limited evidence of FM equivalence, and Table 1 loses uncertainty detail by rounding small standard errors to 0.00.
